analysis.title: 5.5% May Be Just The Beginning: AI Is Changing The Price Of Money
key_insights: The US 10-year yield has broken out of a multi-year range above 5%, with 5.5% the next major level and a potential magnet for yields.
The upper trend line connecting several major highs sits around 5.75-5.80%, and there is little obvious resistance overhead.
Bond vol is still stressed. The MOVE index has retreated from recent highs but rates volatility remains elevated.
Rates and oil have moved closely together since late June. Crude is still elevated and is pushing higher again, which raises the question of what happens to yields if oil accelerates.
Privorotsky argues that post-GFC abundant savings and low rates are ending, while sovereign financing needs and AI demand for capital are both very large.
SpaceX is reportedly seeking $40bn and Broadcom is exploring more than $50bn in financing, adding to supply pressure on capital markets.
If AI generates 20-30% IRRs, borrowing at high single-digit rates makes sense for AI firms. The open question is the effect on everyone else competing for that capital.
Privorotsky sees two outcomes: AI becomes increasingly self-financing, or capital is rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy crack. CCC spreads may already be an early warning.
The US 10-year yield has moved closely with selected hyperscaler CDS spreads, linking AI-driven financing costs to credit stress.
Semiconductor volatility looks relatively cheap against stress in rates and hyperscaler CDS. The Market Ear says hedging spillover risk through semis vol makes sense.

sector_views.rationale: Semis vol looks cheap relative to rates and hyperscaler CDS stress, so the note favors it as a hedge for spillover risk. It does not give a directional equity view.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A breakout from the multi-year range with little overhead resistance. Higher yields raise financing costs for AI-related borrowers and risk straining weaker credits.
